external_entities.name: Member
external_entities.description: A grocery loyalty programme member who uses the mobile app, authorizes partner apps, and has an account.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state the member's trust-zone placement.

processes.name: Mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to sign in, call the rewards API, and manage partner connections.
processes.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app. The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow and then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back.
processes.notes: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone. PKCE support is unknown: "Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge."

processes.name: Authorization server
processes.description: The authorization service that signs members in, issues authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and access tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow

processes.name: Partner app
processes.description: A web application run by another company that can display a member's points and use the authorization service.
processes.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
processes.notes: Partner apps receive client IDs and client secrets and are given every scope.

processes.name: Browser
processes.description: The browser used by a member to sign in to the authorization server and approve consent for a partner app.
processes.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen that lists the scopes.

processes.name: Rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and receives requests authenticated with access tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.
processes.notes: The API does not check which client or audience a token was issued for.

processes.name: Support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: Identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.

data_stores.name: Points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.notes: The ledger records which client made each change, and not which member approved it.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store receiving every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: authorize member
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back

data_flows.name: disconnect partner
data_flows.description: The mobile app initiates disconnection of a partner app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app
data_flows.notes: The text says this deletes the partner app's refresh token from the identity database but does not state the application-level interaction.

data_flows.name: use browser
data_flows.description: A member uses a browser to sign in and approve partner-app consent.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen that lists the scopes.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The browser accesses the authorization server sign-in page and consent screen.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen
data_flows.notes: The authorization-server sign-in is kept in a cookie for thirty days; no idle timeout was decided.

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: The partner app sends token requests containing its client secret in the request body.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.

data_flows.name: take access token
data_flows.description: The support console uses access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: A member uses the support console to close the member's account.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and retrieves identity and authorization data in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: Accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: read-write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write API logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes every request it receives, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: close account record
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: The text states that the member's refresh tokens remain in the same database.

trust_boundaries.name: Our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud-account environment where the system components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account, apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

trust_boundaries.name: Member phone
trust_boundaries.description: The member-controlled phone environment running the mobile app and browser.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account, apart from the members' phones

trust_boundaries.name: Partner app server
trust_boundaries.description: Servers controlled by other companies that run partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the partner apps ... that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because the support console and rewards API are served on the same public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The text states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data because it stores member email addresses, password hashes, tokens, authorization codes, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents include personal information and credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data because it stores member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents are member-related financial and business records.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data because it stores request headers, which include requests carrying access tokens.
assumptions.basis: The store records every request and its headers, while the rewards API receives bearer access tokens.
